body:
# Description

Fixes #5885.

The NVPF diffusivity data in `Chayambuka2022` are tabulated against the positive particle concentration (131 to 15,197 mol/m3, the axis of `D_p.csv`). `NVPF_diffusivity_Chayambuka2022` scaled the stoichiometry by `"Initial concentration in electrolyte [mol.m-3]"` (1000 mol/m3) instead, so it only ever read the dilute end of the table. It now uses `"Maximum concentration in positive electrode [mol.m-3]"` (15,320 mol/m3), as `HC_diffusivity_Chayambuka2022` does for the negative electrode.

| stoichiometry | D on main [m2/s] | D with this PR [m2/s] | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 2.22e-15 | 5.67e-17 | 39x |
| 0.5 | 1.87e-15 | 8.33e-17 | 22x |
| 0.9 | 1.34e-15 | 3.56e-17 | 38x |

With `pybamm.sodium_ion.BasicDFN()` and the default parameters, the 2C discharge capacity to 2.0 V goes from about 1.6 mAh to 1.18 mAh, matching the corrected value in the issue. At 1C it is 2.11 mAh.

Thanks @jmdface for the report.

## Type of change

Bug fix, with an entry under `## Bug fixes` in CHANGELOG.md.

# Important checks:

- [x] No style issues: ruff 0.16.10 format and check, and comment-slop, pass on the changed files
- [x] Tests added that prove fix is effective: `TestChayambuka2022.test_positive_particle_diffusivity` checks the diffusivity at three stoichiometries with `rel=1e-4, abs=0`. It fails on main and passes with the fix. The existing `test_functions` uses `abs=1e-4`, which cannot see this error (its expected positive diffusivity, 1.8700e-15, was the value of the bug), so I corrected that value too.
- [ ] All tests pass: every test file that uses `Chayambuka2022` or `sodium_ion` passes locally (7 passed). I have not run the full `nox -s tests`, so I am relying on CI for the rest.
- [ ] The documentation builds: not run locally, no docs changes
- [x] Code is commented for hard-to-understand areas

commits.messageBody:
The NVPF diffusivity data are tabulated against the positive particle
concentration (131 to 15,197 mol/m3), but NVPF_diffusivity_Chayambuka2022
scaled the stoichiometry by the initial electrolyte concentration
(1000 mol/m3), so it only read the dilute end of the table and the cathode
diffusivity was 20 to 50 times too large. Scale by the positive electrode
maximum concentration, as HC_diffusivity_Chayambuka2022 does for the negative
electrode, and test the values with a relative tolerance.

Fixes #5885

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

  the old absolute tolerance hid.
- Keep only the stoichiometries that test_functions does not already cover in
  test_positive_particle_diffusivity.
- Re-execute the sodium-ion example notebook so its stored outputs use the
  corrected positive particle diffusivity.
- Link the issue as well as the PR in the CHANGELOG entry.
